slides.5.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.5.points.0: ✓ Prosecco: ideal for Aperitivo hour with olives and light bites; Franciacorta: refined choice for oysters, fine seafood and full-course fine dining
slides.5.points.1: ✓ Lambrusco semi-sparkling red: cuts Emilia charcuterie fat; Trento DOC mountain sparkling: pairs with Speck and alpine cheese
slides.5.points.2: ✓ Moscato d'Asti: classic with tiramisu AND Gorgonzola (sweet-salty contrast) — sweet wine isn't only for desserts
slides.5.points.3: ✓ Vin Santo soaked Cantucci biscotti: Tuscany's purest expression of local dessert culture
slides.5.points.4: ✓ Passito di Pantelleria + Sicilian Cannoli; Recioto della Valpolicella + rich chocolate cake
slides.5.points.5: ✓ Marsala: dry style for cooking (Vitello Piccata sauce); sweet style for desserts (Cannoli); Vergine grade for solo sipping with nuts
slides.5.points.6: ✓ Barolo Chinato: bittersweet spiced fortified wine — pairing with 70%+ dark chocolate is the most traditional combination; also served solo as a digestivo
slides.5.points.7: ✓ Occasion drives the choice: Aperitivo → light sparkling; wedding dinner → lightest to richest in sequence; business dinner → neutral safe choices; family meal → high-value everyday
slides.6.title: 🧠 Special Wine Pairing Knowledge Check
quiz.0.question: What is the most common high-end pairing scenario for Franciacorta in Italian fine dining?
quiz.0.options.1: Paired with oysters and fine seafood, or as full-course dinner wine throughout
quiz.0.explanation: Franciacorta's fine bubbles and minerality make it ideal for refined seafood (oysters, lobster), and its complexity is strong enough to accompany a multi-course dinner from start to finish. It plays the 'Champagne role' in Italian fine dining — not for desserts or heavy dishes.
quiz.1.question: What is the most traditional Tuscan local dessert pairing for Vin Santo?
quiz.1.options.2: Cantucci almond biscotti (dipped into Vin Santo)
quiz.1.explanation: Dipping Cantucci almond biscotti into Vin Santo is Tuscany's most traditional dessert culture — the sweet wine softens the hard biscuit, the biscuit absorbs the wine's nutty-caramel aromas. A pure expression of local culinary identity.
quiz.2.question: What is the most traditional food pairing for Barolo Chinato?
quiz.2.explanation: Barolo Chinato is a bittersweet spiced fortified wine based on Barolo. Its complex bitterness from quinine bark and gentian root creates a perfect bittersweet contrast with 70%+ dark chocolate — Piemonte's most traditional digestivo pairing.
quiz.3.question: Which of the following statements about pairing sweet wine with food is INCORRECT?
quiz.3.options.0: Moscato d'Asti can pair with Gorgonzola blue cheese (sweet-salty contrast)
quiz.3.options.1: Sweet wine can only be paired with desserts and must never be paired with savoury food
quiz.3.options.2: Passito di Pantelleria with Sicilian Cannoli is a traditional regional pairing
quiz.3.options.3: Off-dry Lambrusco can be paired with Prosciutto di Parma (sweet meets salty)
quiz.3.explanation: Pairing sweet wine with savoury food is traditional wisdom, not a taboo: Moscato with Gorgonzola (sweet-salty contrast), Passito with Cannoli (regional native pairing), and Lambrusco with ham (sweetness balances saltiness) are all correct. Only 'sweet wine can only pair with desserts' is wrong.
